reviewNotes: Not the Egbema of Delta State (Warri North and Warri South-West), who are an Ijaw (Izon) clan with a separate history.
Other Rivers Egbema towns named locally (Aggah, Ukpazi, Ekpe Aggah, Ekpe Mgbede, Ugada) are not yet located in GRID3. In Imo, Abacheke and Abaezi are named as Egbema but not yet located.
In Ogba/Egbema/Ndoni the Egbema hold about 2 of 17 wards (Wikipedia), so the stripes show a shared homeland, not equal shares.
name: Egbema

language.name: Egbema
language.note: Glottolog lists Egbema as a dialect within Igbo.

summary.text: The Egbema are one people whose kingdom was split by the state boundary: most of their towns lie in Ohaji/Egbema LGA of Imo State, around the LGA headquarters at Mmahu, and the rest in Ogba/Egbema/Ndoni LGA of Rivers State, around Mgbede, Okwuzi and Ebocha. Local histories describe the kingdom as “balkanized politically but traditionally one”, and trace its origin to a migration from old Benin. They speak Egbema, which Glottolog counts within Igbo. Their land holds major oil and gas facilities.

areas.note: Five of the LGA’s eleven wards are Egbema A to E; the rest are Ohaji.
One of the LGA’s three founding peoples, with the Ogba and the Ndoni.
